title: Rolling Reserve Shadow Roster and De-scope Decision Canvas
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a lightweight, reproducible playbook and scheduling experiment for rolling reserve (shadow roster) allocation and a decision canvas for mid-cycle scope cuts. Context: we want a low-friction operational pattern that reduces ad-hoc firefighting when spikes or feature work collide with limited staff. This ticket covers: 1) a template for creating 'reserve bands' — small staffed buffers rotated across teams; 2) a shadow roster schedule and pairing rules for on-call/coverage swaps; 3) a decision canvas that PMs and Eng leads can use to consistently evaluate scope trims (impact, dependencies, customer risk); 4) a runbook for executing a mid-cycle de-scope including comms and release gating. Deliverables: - Reserve band definition doc (size, eligibility, trigger thresholds) - Shadow roster schedule: rotation cadence, pairing rules, handoff checklist - Decision canvas template (CSV/Confluence/Slack workflow) - Runbook for executing a scoped de-scope (notifying stakeholders, updating backlog, hotfix vs defer criteria) Acceptance criteria: - Playbook reviewed by Eng leads, Design, and Support - Pilot plan for Cycle 2026-W10 with at least 2 teams enrolled - Templates published in Confluence with example filled canvases - Metrics to evaluate pilot defined (time-to-recover incidents, % of capacity freed by de-scope, decision latency) Links: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Rolling+Reserve+Playbook Example decision canvas: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExampleDriveLink GitHub scheduling helper (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/7890
